newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-CZECH TEAM HIT BY CURSE OF THE WRONG SHIRTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CZECH TEAM HIT BY CURSE OF THE WRONG SHIRTS.

text.p: Milan Boksa, the coach of Czech first division side Petra Drnovice took a leaf right out of Alex Ferguson's book on Monday when he said his team lost a league match on Sunday -- because they were wearing the wrong colour shirts.
Boksa spoke after his team went down 3-0 to Ceske Budejovice in thick fog and he claimed they couldn't see each other because they had dark blue shirts on.

Fog engulfed the pitch during the top-of-the table clash between the sides making vision at times difficult on the field, and nearly impossible off it. And after his team lost to Ceske, who were wearing white shirts with black facings, Boksa said: "We should have had different strips. Our dark blue ones made it difficult to see each other. At least that's the way it looked to me."

Last April Ferguson said the reason why his Manchester United side were trailing by 3-0 at halftime in a league match at Southampton was because their grey shirts made it difficult for his players to see each other against the crowd. They changed to blue at half-time but still lost the match 3-1.

That was the last time United ever wore those colours, but if Boksa wants an omen, he can look for one in that United recovered from that defeat and went on to win the cup and league double in England last season.
Slovan Liberec stayed three points clear at the top after beating lowly Karvina 1-0 thanks to a 73rd minute penalty from Ludek Klusacek.
